message: AutoHotkey v1 command syntax with a comma. Version 2 calls functions: MsgBox("text").
AutoHotkey v2 does not expand %var% inside quotes, so this string is stored literally. Join instead: "total " count.
This script is pinned to AutoHotkey v1, so every v2 snippet in this pack will fail to load here.
A TOML inline table may not end with a trailing comma. The parser stops on this line.
TOML rejects an integer with a leading zero. Write 9, or quote it as "09" if it is a code.
Nothing but a comment may follow a TOML table header on the same line.
This DeviceTree property is not closed with a semicolon, and the compiler will report the error on a later line.
DeviceTree accepts only "okay" or "disabled" here. Anything else leaves the node switched off at boot.
Node names use hyphens, not underscores, under the Devicetree naming rules. Labels may keep the underscore.
@ConfigProperty with no defaultValue makes the key mandatory, and deployment fails when it is missing in one environment.
@Retry with no maxRetries falls back to the default of 3. State the number so the retry budget is visible to a reviewer.
A Ren'Py label must end with a colon, otherwise the script fails to parse at launch.
This Ren'Py line is indented with a tab. Script files must use spaces, or the game refuses to start.
A force-unwrapped URL crashes the app on a malformed address. Use guard let and throw instead.
try! turns a thrown error into a crash. Use try with a catch, or try? when nil is acceptable.
return inside forEach leaves only that closure and the loop keeps going. Use a for loop when you mean to stop.
An Inkling ranged number is written with two dots, not a comma: number<0 .. 1>.
This file targets Inkling 1.x, and the graph and concept snippets in this pack are 2.0.
A credential is written straight into this file. Move it to an environment variable or a file the repository ignores.
This workflow step is not pinned to a version, so it can change under you. Add a tag such as @v4 or a commit SHA.
An .editorconfig boolean is lower-case. True is read as an unknown value and the setting is skipped.
Semantic highlighting is switched off here, so the Python semantic colour rules in this pack never take effect.
